subject: Infra onramp: account provisioning, peering, and network sanity checks
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthtech-ops.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@healthtech-ops.com
Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: Redwood private deployment (HealthTech Labs)

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. We're ready to begin the private deployment onboarding for HealthTech Labs. High-level ask: we want a VPC-based private deployment in our AWS account (us-east-1) with a dedicated GPU pool for inference of our internal models.

Primary kickoff items from our side:
- Provide Redwood's account prerequisites and naming conventions so our infra team can provision the right IAM/service accounts and subnets.
- Confirm required peering/Transit GW configuration and recommended route table entries for secure egress to S3 + KMS.
- Clarify the KMS/HSM expectations (customer-managed KMS) and key rotation cadence.

Attached: HTL network inventory (subnet ranges, account id), and a preliminary list of hosts that will need access.

Can we schedule a 45-min tech onboarding on Wednesday? Timezones: PST.

Best,
Carlos
Carlos Vega
Cloud Operations Lead
HealthTech Labs

Attachments: htl_network_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthtech-ops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Redwood private deployment (HealthTech Labs)

Carlos — thanks, appreciate the inventory. Wed 11/29 10am PST works for us.

I'm looping in Marissa (eng lead for onprem/VPC activations), Vivek (network/oncall), and Kimberly (security & KMS). Below is the minimal action list we'll use to prepare the account — this is our operational checklist in brief. I'll send the longer playbook after this thread.

Redwood minimal account prerequisites (to provision before the call):
1) AWS account ID & org unit + a naming prefix for resources.
2) VPC peering or Transit Gateway ID if you prefer central routing. Please expose private CIDR ranges and any overlapping segments.
3) Service accounts: one runner/service account for the Redwood control-plane (policy: minimal privileges), one KMS-encrypted S3 role for model artifacts, and a CI/CD deploy principal. Template attached (sfeed-service-account-template.txt).
4) KMS: customer-managed symmetric key with "EnableKeyRotation" true and an attached policy that allows Redwood account principal to Encrypt/Decrypt for inference keys.
5) Egress: NAT or proxy egress IP(s) for allowlisting (we'll provide HA pair IPs).
6) Firewall/ACL: allow ports 443 outbound to our streamer endpoints; inbound only for SSM/jumpbox if you want remote debug.

Preflight network sanity checks we usually run during onboarding:
- BGP/peering validation (Route propagation + overlapping CIDR checks)
- DNS resolution for private hostnames (we recommend Route53 private hosted zones)
- MTU path-check for model pulls (> 9000 can be problematic with some NIC drivers)
- KMS policy handshake (we'll attempt a test encrypt/decrypt during the call)

I'll bring an activation checklist and sample Terraform snippets to the call.

See you Wed.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sfeed-service-account-template.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthtech-ops.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Redwood private deployment (HealthTech Labs)

All — quick note to align on the run-of-play for Wednesday's session (45 min):
- 0–10m: Introductions + roles (who owns what on HTL side)
- 10–20m: Account inventory review (VPC, subnets, security groups, NACLs)
- 20–35m: KMS + S3 access test (we'll attempt a sample object encrypt/decrypt and model artefact pull)
- 35–45m: Next steps + roll plan (canary traffic, smoke tests, fallback model policy)

Pre-assignments for Redwood: I'll bring the activation playbook and the minimal Terraform module for peering + route table changes. Vivek will run the network traceroute/mtu checks and propose a temporary allowlist IP for egress.

HTL action items to complete before the call (please have these available in the call):
- Confirm the exact AWS account ID and VPC IDs.
- Provide IAM contact and the principal ARN we should use to test KMS.
- Share any corporate proxy / egress constraints (we can work around proxies but need the host/IP allowlist).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Enablement Engineer — Private Deploys
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_account_prereqs_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthtech-ops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Redwood private deployment (HealthTech Labs)

Thanks — we reconfirmed the list. Quick responses inline:
- AWS account: 123456789012 (production-sandpit). VPCs: vpc-0a1b2c3d (apps), vpc-0f9e8d7c (data). No overlapping CIDR with Redwood (we checked).
- IAM contact: @sasha (sasha@healthtech-ops.com). We'll provide the principal ARN before EOD.
- Corporate proxy: outbound proxy at 54.213.111.22 (we can allowlist).

Attached is the signed MSA (DocuSign) and a short network inventory with a few NAT IPs.

See you at 10am.

— Carlos

Attachments: DOCUSIGN:ABC-HTL-2028-11-27 (signed contract)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthtech-ops.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-call: network sanity results + temporary allowlist

Folks — follow-up from the call and the checks we ran during the session:
- Peering/Routes: Verified route propagation from vpc-0a1b2c3d -> Transit-GW. No overlapping CIDR detected.
- MTU: Detected an MTU mismatch on one of the peered edges (path MTU 1500 in one hop, 9000 on others). Recommend pinning jumbo frames to 1500 for the Redwood model pulls or enabling MSS clamping on the gateway.
- DNS: Private hosted zone resolution worked for internal hostnames.
- KMS handshake: Successfully performed test encrypt/decrypt using the supplied test principal (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rdw-deploy-test-role).

Temporary egress allowlist for Redwood ephemeral control-plane IPs (for initial onboarding only):
- 3.120.45.18
- 3.120.45.19

Next operational steps from Redwood side:
1) We'll submit a short Terraform change set for the peering/route additions (JIRA:INFRAONRAMP-452).
2) Provide a runbook for the MTU workaround and an egress checklist for HTL infra to approve.
3) Schedule a smoke traffic window for model pull and a canary run (suggest Thu 11/30 09:00 PST).

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Infra onramp: account provisioning, peering, and network sanity checks

Carlos — great session, thanks to your team for being prepared. Quick summary and asks for closure before we move to canary: 

Checklist to close (HTL):
- Apply the Terraform peering + route-change PR and mark it "ready for review" (JIRA:INFRAONRAMP-452).
- Approve temporary egress allowlist IPs in your firewall (3.120.45.18/19) for a 48-hour window.
- Confirm the deploy/test principal ARN via email to sasha@healthtech-ops.com and copy us so we can run one final KMS validation.
- Confirm a canary window (we propose Thu 11/30 09:00 PST).

Redwood deliverables:
- PR with Terraform module + sample peering configuration (by EOD).
- MTU runbook + recommendation doc (by tomorrow morning).
- Canary checklist (smoke tests, rollback steps, health-check queries).

If we get these closed, we should be able to move to an initial smoke canary and have the dedicated GPU pool accept traffic by end of next week.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
